context: Second composite, built entirely from signals characterized in the verified signal library (V2/strategies/signal_library.py, look-ahead-verified for IBS and boundary-corrected for all 9). Different design from composite_v1: price-based mean-reversion signals (IBS, RSI2) rather than trend/momentum signals, weekly rebalance with a harder holdout window (2019-2025, the period where IBS's own subsample analysis already showed decay to t=2.60). This is the third and final holdout consumption of the original 3-slot budget.
universe: Full Sharadar PIT eligible universe: common stock, major US exchanges, price>=$1, trailing 63-day median dollar volume>=$500K, >=252 days history, excluding Finance, Real Estate, Healthcare by Fama `sector` field (same convention as the signal library exercise). ~1,300-1,600 eligible names/day.

hard_exclusions.nsi_q5: Bottom quintile (Q5) on trailing-365-day sharesbas (MRQ) percent change, same ascending-sort convention as net_share_issuance.py. Computed ONCE PER CALENDAR MONTH (at the first weekly rebalance of the month) and held fixed for every Friday rebalance within that month -- not recomputed weekly. This avoids repeated fundamentals queries and matches the fact that the underlying quarterly/trailing-annual data doesn't change week to week.
hard_exclusions.quality_q5: Bottom quintile (Q5) on the 6-component quality composite score (quality.py convention). Same monthly-cached computation as NSI Q5.
hard_exclusions.note: Excluded names receive no composite score and are ineligible for the portfolio for the rest of that calendar month, regardless of how they'd score on A/B/C/D.

composite_score.signal_A_ibs: weight 0.50. score_A_raw = 1 - mean(IBS over trailing 5 trading days), where IBS=(close-low)/(high-low). Percentile-ranked (ascending) across the eligible non-excluded universe on that Friday -- high score = closed near the daily low, averaged over the week, i.e. persistent oversold-ness.
composite_score.signal_B_rsi2: weight 0.30. score_B_raw = 100 - RSI(close,2). Percentile-ranked (ascending) across the eligible non-excluded universe -- high score = most oversold on the fast RSI2 measure.
composite_score.signal_C_sector_rotation: weight 0.15. rs = close/close[-63] - 1. Percentile-ranked (ascending) WITHIN each stock's own Fama sector (not globally) -- high score = strongest trailing-63-day relative strength versus same-sector peers.
composite_score.signal_D_friday_down_bonus: weight 0.05, binary (not percentile-ranked -- a 0/1 indicator is already on a comparable 0-1 scale, and percentile-ranking a binary field breaks down under ties, as found with composite_v1's Turnaround Tuesday exclusion attempt). score_D = 1 if that Friday's own daily return < -1%, else 0. Restated from the original Monday-specific Turnaround Tuesday concept to fit a Friday-close-only rebalance structure: a stock down >1% on the rebalance Friday itself is a Monday-bounce candidate.
composite_score.composite: 0.50*score_A + 0.30*score_B + 0.15*score_C + 0.05*score_D, computed only for eligible non-excluded stocks.

portfolio_construction.holding: Top quintile (top 20% of eligible non-excluded names), equal weight.
portfolio_construction.execution: Following Monday open -- one session of execution lag versus the Friday-close signal. Both entry and exit legs of each weekly holding period use Monday-open prices (i.e. the return series is open-to-open, lagged one trading session behind the Friday signal), applied consistently roll-to-roll.

cost_model.basis: 10bps round-trip on weekly turnover, measured from actual portfolio holdings changes (symmetric-difference-of-holdings convention, one-way, matching prior strategies).
cost_model.note: cost>5%/yr is treated as FALSIFIED regardless of alpha, not merely flagged.

regression_sanity_checks.long_only: R2 > 0.4 and 0.5 < market_beta < 1.5. If either fails: stop and investigate before reading any alpha number.

holdout_rationale: IBS's own subsample analysis (signal library exercise) showed decay to t=2.60 in 2019-2024. Using 2019-2025 as holdout deliberately tests the composite in the already-known-weaker regime -- a harder test than composite_v1's holdout, chosen specifically because it is less likely to be flattered by a favorable draw.

falsification_criteria.primary_pass_advance_to_holdout: alpha t>2.0 AND annualized cost<3%/yr AND R2<0.90 AND small-cap alpha > large-cap alpha AND both preregistered development sub-periods (2001-2009, 2010-2018) individually show positive alpha
falsification_criteria.secondary_suggestive_no_holdout: t between 1.5 and 2.0 with positive alpha, OR cost between 3-5%/yr with positive alpha
falsification_criteria.falsified: t<1.5, OR alpha negative, OR cost>5%/yr, OR either development sub-period shows negative alpha (recorded as REGIME_DEPENDENT, does not advance regardless of overall t-stat)
falsification_criteria.no_rmw_criterion: Unlike composite_v1, there is no RMW-sign criterion. Composite_v1's RMW failure was diagnosed as a mechanical consequence of buying recent losers (a price-signal composite), not evidence of factor replication -- RMW loading here is expected to be negative or near zero by construction, and is not a pass/fail gate.

subperiod_analysis.requirement: BOTH must show positive alpha (not merely t-stat direction) to advance to holdout. A single negative sub-period is recorded as REGIME_DEPENDENT and blocks holdout advancement regardless of pooled development-period significance -- this is the check composite_v1 lacked, whose apparent edge was concentrated entirely in 2001-2016 small-cap conditions.

benchmarks.secondary: Portfolio A (equal-weight full universe, test1_portfolio_A.csv), dev/holdout-period subset, active alpha via long-short-convention regression
benchmarks.tertiary: SPY, raw CAGR difference over the aligned period

holdout_budget_note: This is holdout consumption 3 of the original 3-slot budget. After this test, no holdout slots remain -- any future composite attempt requires a completely fresh signal-development track, not further iteration on this one.
constraints: Preregistration committed before any data is touched.
Development sub-period check is mandatory before the holdout decision; both sub-periods must be individually positive, regardless of pooled t-stat.
Identical configuration for holdout -- no parameter changes after seeing development results.
Cost flag checked and reported before alpha numbers.
If development is FALSIFIED: record it, do not run holdout, do not modify weights, archive.
If holdout FAILS: record it, do not iterate -- holdout budget is exhausted.
If holdout PASSES: report and stop -- no live system started without explicit further instruction.
